record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.context_brief: Observable sensitivity and general medium response
record.original_question: Which aspects of fluctuating initial conditions is each final-state observable most sensitive to, and can a general characterization of hydrodynamic medium response be developed well enough to place significant constraints on both initial conditions and quark-gluon-plasma medium properties?

evidence.quote:
Motivated by the large uncertainties that still remain in the initial conditions,
another emerging theme is the characterization of the medium response in a general
way. A more detailed understanding of hydrodynamic response to initial conditions, as
well as a precise determination of which aspects of the initial conditions each observable
is most sensitive to, would allow for significant constraints to be placed on the properties
of the initial conditions [24] and medium properties [25].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled by an event-by-event fluctuating initial energy/entropy density profile $\varepsilon(\mathbf{x}_\perp)$ in the transverse plane, characterized by its eccentricity harmonics $\varepsilon_n e^{i n \Phi_n} = -\int d^2 x_\perp\, r^2 e^{i n \phi}\,\varepsilon(\mathbf{x}_\perp) / \int d^2 x_\perp\, r^2\, \varepsilon(\mathbf{x}_\perp)$, $n \geq 2$, together with higher-order cumulant moments and longitudinal/rapidity fluctuations. Suppose this initial state evolves under relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with transport coefficients (shear viscosity $\eta/s$, bulk viscosity $\zeta/s$, equation of state, relaxation times) characterizing the quark–gluon plasma medium, and freezes out into final-state hadrons whose azimuthal distribution is described by the flow harmonics $v_n e^{i n \Psi_n}$ and their multi-particle cumulants and event-plane correlations.

(a) For each final-state observable $\mathcal{O}$ in the set $\{v_n,\ \langle v_n^2\rangle,\ v_n\{2k\}\text{ cumulants},\ \text{symmetric cumulants } \mathrm{SC}(m,n),\ \text{event-plane correlators }\langle\cos(\sum c_i n_i \Psi_{n_i})\rangle,\ \text{rapidity-dependent flow correlations}\}$, identify precisely which features (linear eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$, nonlinear mixings $\varepsilon_m \varepsilon_k$, event-plane angles $\Phi_n$, higher cumulants of the initial geometry, longitudinal decorrelations) determine $\mathcal{O}$ to leading and subleading order, and quantify the corresponding response coefficients.

(b) Develop a general (model-independent) characterization of the hydrodynamic medium response—mapping initial-state characteristics to final-state observables—sufficient to simultaneously place quantitatively significant, well-defined constraints on (i) the statistical properties of the fluctuating initial conditions and (ii) the QGP transport coefficients.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open research program in heavy-ion physics. Substantial progress has been made (linear and cubic response relations $v_n \approx \kappa_n \varepsilon_n$ for $n=2,3$, nonlinear mode-coupling for $v_4, v_5$, Bayesian global analyses constraining $\eta/s(T)$ and $\zeta/s(T)$, symmetric cumulants and event-plane correlations distinguishing initial-state models), but a complete general characterization simultaneously fixing initial conditions and medium properties remains incomplete and active as of the mid-2020s.

status_evidence.title: Bayesian constraints on the QGP shear and bulk viscosities
status_evidence.snippet: Global Bayesian analyses of heavy-ion data constrain transport coefficients but residual uncertainties from the initial state remain.
status_evidence.claim: The simultaneous determination of initial conditions and medium transport coefficients is still subject to significant uncertainties, indicating the program is partially advanced but not closed.
